bull.t: Favorable FDA safety review allows dosing to resume
bull.b: A no-comments FDA safety review is a durable de-risking event: it validates the company’s safety monitoring and protocol changes, enables continuation of clinical programs across indications, and preserves the ability to generate pivotal data and regulatory feedback over the next 2–6 months.

New gross proceeds that extend runway into 2H 2027 materially increase the company’s ability to fund planned Phase 1b and IND-enabling work without immediate capital markets access, supporting program execution and reducing short-term financing disruption risk.

bull.t: Improving loss trend and stabilized burn
bull.b: A multi-year narrowing of net losses and more stable TTM cash burn suggests improving cost discipline and operational efficiency. That trend increases predictability of funding needs and supports executing clinical milestones with lower incremental cash requirements.

bear.t: Negative stockholders’ equity weakens balance sheet
bear.b: Negative equity is a persistent structural weakness that reduces financial flexibility, may limit borrowing capacity, and signals cumulative losses have eroded capital. Over the medium term this raises the company’s dependence on dilutive financings and constrains strategic options.

bear.t: Sustained heavy cash burn and no revenue
bear.b: Consistent ~-$21M annual operating cash burn with no product revenue creates an enduring financing requirement. This structural cash gap means program continuity depends on repeated external funding, increasing execution risk if markets or investor appetite tighten.

bear.t: High dilution risk from loan amendments and warrants
bear.b: Contractual expansion of lender conversion rights, repriced and new warrants, and large warrant overhang from the placement create a durable dilution overhang. This can erode existing equity value, complicate future financings, and affect long-term shareholder returns even if clinical milestones are met.
